brief.topic: A Quiet Shape That Keeps the Same Width

s01: Watch the space between these two rails.
As this shape turns,
the rails never move.
The shape is not a circle,
yet it fits the same gap in every direction.
This is a Reuleaux triangle.
Its secret begins with an ordinary equilateral triangle.
All three sides have the same length.
Put a compass at one corner,
and draw the arc between the other two.
Repeat from each corner.
Three equal circular arcs make our rounded triangle.
Now look at these two contact points.
One is a corner.
The opposite point lies on the arc drawn from that very corner.
The distance between them is the compass radius:
exactly the original side length.
Turn a little.
The contact slides along the same arc,
but that radius does not change.
Turn further,
and another corner takes over.
The roles change;
the width does not.
This is what constant width means:
the distance between parallel supporting lines stays the same.
It does not mean every point on the edge
is equally far from the center.
So putting an axle at this center
would not make an ordinary smooth wheel.
A circle has that extra property.
The rounded triangle offers something different:
a small reminder that one familiar property need not belong
to one familiar shape.
Geometry gives us room for alternatives.
